decision: Use split, bounded evidence collectors for dom0 policy and coordinator service identity, then assemble the existing verified deployment artifact offline.

winner.correctness: Policy evidence is read only from persistent /etc/qubes/policy.d and coordinator evidence is collected only under the expected non-root service EUID. Assembly preserves source separation before the existing artifact verifier checks exact allow-then-deny policy and service target binding.
winner.robustnessSecurity: No shell execution, no qrexec mutation, bounded input files, no symlink policy files, immutable canonical qrexec handler locations, immutable target/marker/directory checks under the service identity, and no override that weakens production path checks for tests.
winner.latencyResources: Two bounded local file captures plus metadata/access checks; no daemon, watcher, database, WAL, persistent process, or extra qrexec round trip.
winner.regressionRisk: Reuses the existing deployment artifact verifier and manifest builder rather than introducing a second readiness authority.
winner.qa: Unit tests cover assembly, effective-UID fail-closed behavior, canonical handler path enforcement, persistent dom0 policy location enforcement, and identity mismatch rejection. Real filesystem success remains intentionally gated to a Qubes deployment because host-temp paths must not bypass canonical path checks.

rejected.reason: Proves intended configuration but not that evidence came from the actual dom0 policy and coordinator service identity.

rejected.approach: single privileged collector spanning dom0 and coordinator state
rejected.reason: Would require broader privilege/transport and collapse independent trust boundaries into one process.

rejected.approach: test-only path override for coordinator collector
rejected.reason: Would create a production-accessible bypass of canonical qrexec handler path enforcement solely to simplify host tests.
Adds lifecycle, IPC, memory, and privileged attack surface without improving the provenance of the two deployment artifacts.

failuresLessons: Verifier strength is not enough when evidence is still manually constructed; collection provenance must be explicit.
A test seam must not weaken the same path/identity boundary being qualified; deployment-only success evidence is preferable to a bypassable unit test.
dom0 and coordinator evidence should remain independently collectible and combinable so compromise or drift in one side is visible rather than hidden by a monolithic collector.
safety: Read-only defensive Qubes qualification only; no financial transaction, payment data, fraud workflow, or security-control weakening.
